chunks: Abu Ayyub asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who transfers a debt to another man by means of property: can recourse be made against him? He said:
No, recourse is never made against him at all, unless he had already become bankrupt before that.

key_terms.بِالْمَالِ: with respect to the financial obligation or debt
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: recourse is made back against someone for payment
key_terms.يُحِيلُ: transfers a debt or liability to another person

ai.seo_question: Does the original debtor remain liable after transferring a debt to another person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on hawalah, the transfer of a debt obligation from one person to another. It states that once the transfer is valid, the original party is no longer liable, except in the case where the transferee had already been bankrupt before the transfer.
